script: In May 1941, the German battleship Bismarck sank with over two thousand men aboard - and sailors swore a ship's cat survived it, found floating on a plank. A British destroyer, HMS Cossack, fished him out and adopted him. Five months later, a torpedo sank the Cossack too. He was rescued again and placed aboard the aircraft carrier Ark Royal. Three weeks after that, a German U-boat sank the Ark Royal as well. Three warships, one cat, all gone within six months. The surviving crew started calling him Unsinkable Sam. The Bismarck and Cossack legs come from the sailors' own telling - but the Ark Royal rescue is the one every historian agrees is real, photographed by British newspapers in 1941. After that, the Royal Navy made a decision: he had used up his luck, and he would never serve at sea again. He spent the next fourteen years on dry land in Belfast and never set foot on a ship again. metadata.title: Random But True: The Cat Three Warships Couldn't Sink
metadata.caption:
In May 1941, the German battleship Bismarck sank with over two thousand men aboard - and sailors swore a ship's cat survived it, found floating on a plank and picked up by the British destroyer HMS Cossack.

Five months later, a torpedo sank the Cossack too. The cat was rescued again and placed aboard the aircraft carrier Ark Royal - and three weeks after that, a German U-boat sank the Ark Royal as well.

Three warships, one cat, all gone within six months. The surviving crew started calling him Unsinkable Sam.

The Bismarck and Cossack legs of the story come from the sailors' own telling. The Ark Royal rescue is the part every historian agrees is real - it was photographed and made British newspapers in 1941.

After that, the Royal Navy decided he'd used up his luck and would never serve at sea again. He spent the next fourteen years on dry land in Belfast and died there in 1955.
